emma_cs: Quick check-in on AcmeCorp account — noticed a ~3x increase in error rate over the last 24h. Dashboard breakdown: ~45% 5xx (model timeouts), ~35% upstream timeouts, ~20% rate_limit responses. Top failing endpoints observed: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/embeddings. Token spend up ~18% and p95 latency jumped from ~480ms to ~1.2s. Sharing snippets below for triage.
liam_re: I'll take backend triage. Can you paste a representative request and a failing response?
emma_cs: sample request pasted below — this is what customer ran for the embed migration.
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}'
```
liam_re: Got it. Reproduced locally, seeing repeated 502/504 from pool b-3.
anika_ops: Checking infra logs now — lots of upstream 504s and connection resets on b-3. Nginx keepalive is dropping connections after ~60s; kernel shows TCP retransmit spikes. Possibly long-running requests + connection churn from the batch job.
sre-bot: [ALERT] ALRT-1234 rate_limit_exceeded — account: acme-corp, window: 12h, events: 1,240, soft limit breached. Link: https://redwood.infra/alerts/ALRT-1234
liam_re: If the customer kicked off a big embedding migration that would explain the burst. Michael, did Acme tell you they'd run anything?
michael_sales: Yes they started a large embedding migration around 03:10 UTC yesterday, but they didn't request throughput increases. Renewal conversation next week — need to flag this as potential churn risk if we don't help stabilize.
jordan_ce: Can we get a short customer-facing summary (cause, what we're doing, ETA to normal) so CS can message them? They want something concise.
emma_cs: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) temporary soft rate-limit increase for AcmeCorp to 2x for next 24h; 2) patch nginx keepalive to 300s on pool b-3 and restart workers (reduce resets); 3) enable model-fallback to gpt-medium variant for time-sensitive routes to reduce tail latency; 4) ops run a short-scale test. Who can own the rate-limit bump?
anika_ops: I can rollout nginx keepalive patch to staging now and schedule prod within the hour if CI stable. Will post PR. Need infra lead approval for rate-limit bump.
ops-bot: Deploy queued: infra/keepalive-patch v2026.3 — CI passed, awaiting manual approval.
liam_re: I'll reach out to infra leads for the temporary limit bump and create a small dashboard showing errors by endpoint + pool. Also will add a filter for 'embedding migration' traffic to validate cause.
emma_cs: I'll draft the one-paragraph customer note and share before sending. Action items: Emma -> customer note, Liam -> dashboard + infra approval, Anika -> nginx patch rollout, Michael -> prepare renewal context. ETA: initial mitigation (keepalive + rate bump) target within 2 hours, full stability within 8-12 hours. Thanks all :thumbsup:
